title: Pairs With an Exact Gap
statement:
`numbers` is sorted from smallest to largest and all numbers are **different**. Count the pairs of numbers whose **difference is exactly `gap`** (the larger minus the smaller). `gap` is at least `1`.

A pair is two different positions; the pair (a, b) and (b, a) count as one.

hints.nudge: For one number, the partner you want is a single value: number + gap. Because the list is sorted, how can you find it without searching from scratch each time?
hints.pattern: Two pointers that only move forward: for each left number, advance the right pointer until the difference is at least gap.
hints.pseudocode:
j = 0; count = 0
for i in 0..n-1:
  if j <= i: j = i + 1
  while j < n and numbers[j] - numbers[i] < gap: j += 1
  if j < n and numbers[j] - numbers[i] == gap: count += 1
return count
hints.walkthrough: Checking every pair is O(n^2). Fix the smaller number numbers[i]. Its partner must be exactly numbers[i] + gap; since all numbers are different there is at most one such partner. As i moves to the right, the number you look for gets larger, so the position j of the partner never moves left: keep j between rounds and only push it forward while the difference is still smaller than the gap. After the loop, either numbers[j] - numbers[i] equals the gap (one pair found) or it is larger (no partner for this i). Both pointers only move forward: O(n). (A hash set of the numbers also gives O(n), but the sorted order lets you use O(1) memory.)
